confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'it is highly likely that the drain pump motor itself is failing intermittently'

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'I would recommend calling out an appliance repair engineer to replace the drain pump for you.'

rationale: The assistant fixated on the drain pump from the second turn, never asked about the flashing light pattern or error code, never considered a control board or pressure system fault, and declared pump failure 'highly likely' on evidence (intermittent stall, pump runs briefly then stops, normal draining on good washes) that is equally consistent with a pressure switch or board fault. It re-asked the drain hose check after the customer had already said the hose was fine and into a standpipe, prompting the customer to complain, and a service outage cost another turn. Safety was fine (unplug before reaching in) and it did ultimately refer to an engineer, but framed the visit as a pump replacement rather than diagnosis, which the ground truth says is unjustified.
